_README: Hand-written GOLDEN archival Q&A set for step_7/eval/eval.py (the RAG/answer evaluator).
These ~12 questions are the *trusted* yardstick: real questions a Solanus archivist or a
petitioner's descendant would actually ask. They were authored by reading the corpus, NOT by an
LLM. (eval.py ALSO ships a SYNTHETIC generator that can mint more questions in this exact shape,
but it is gated OFF — David's labels are the authority; a machine never silently grows the gold
set. See eval.py:synthesize_golden_questions.)
SCHEMA per item (every field optional except 'id' + 'question'):
id            stable id (so results join across runs).
question      the natural-language query handed to retrieval + generation.
category      what KIND of archival ask it is (lookup / aggregate / relational / temporal / ...).
difficulty    simple | moderate | complex  (should roughly match retrieval.route_query).
ground_truth  a short reference answer sketch. Used ONLY by answer_relevancy / similarity if an
LLM judge is enabled; faithfulness/ctx-precision do NOT need it (they judge vs the
retrieved context, RAGAS-style). Left honest + terse; the corpus is the authority.
expected_where  a metadata pre-filter that SHOULD bound the relevant set (passed straight to
retrieval RetrievalConfig.where). Lets context-recall be estimated for free,
with no human-labeled passage ids, by asking 'did we retrieve from this slice?'.
relevant_doc_ids  OPTIONAL hand-labeled list of source doc_ids that truly answer this. When
present, context precision/recall are computed EXACTLY against it (no LLM).
Empty by default — David fills these in as he verifies, turning the free
proxy metric into a hard one. (Per project rule: gold is David-only.)
stresses      which metric this question is designed to exercise, so a low score is diagnostic.
notes         why this question is here / what makes it hard.

questions.question: What favors were reported for cancer around 1945?
questions.ground_truth: Notebook entries record petitioners enrolled in the Seraphic Mass Association for cancer; some report the condition improved or 'cured' after enrollment. The exact 1945 set must be read from the entries; year comes from the page archival date, not the entry.
questions.notes: The canonical archival ask. Hard because 'cancer' is a CONDITION entity and '1945' lives in the page-level archv_date, not the entry text (see stages/normalize_dates.py A2). Tests whether temporal + condition retrieval find the right slice.

questions.question: Find all Casey-family correspondence in the archive.
questions.ground_truth: Letters to/from members of the Casey family (Solanus's own relatives). Requires entity resolution to group surname + given-name variants into the Casey family cluster.
questions.notes: Exercises entity grouping (RESEARCH_PLAN A3): 'Casey' as a family, not a string. A good answer should NOT pull every letter that merely mentions the word 'Casey'.

questions.question: Which petitioners came from Detroit?
questions.ground_truth: People whose location (sender location / origin / entry text) is Detroit, Michigan. Both letters (src_location_sender / src_origin) and notebook entries can carry the place.
questions.notes: PLACE entity grounding. Detroit is the home city (St. Bonaventure Monastery), so it is common — precision matters more than recall here.

questions.question: When was Father Solanus Casey born?
questions.ground_truth: November 25, 1870 (Bernard Francis Casey, Oak Grove, Wisconsin). This is biography, not necessarily in the letters/notebooks; a faithful system may abstain if no source region supports it.
questions.notes: A 'simple' route. Deliberately tests ABSTENTION: if the corpus has no supporting region, the grounded answer is 'not found in the archive' — a faithful system must NOT confabulate the well-known date.

questions.question: What was the Seraphic Mass Association and how were people enrolled in it?
questions.ground_truth: A Capuchin mission-support association; Solanus enrolled petitioners (living and deceased) in it as the spiritual remedy he offered, recording enrollments and later outcomes in his notebooks.
questions.notes: Tests synthesis across many entries that mention enrollment. The phrase recurs constantly, so retrieval is easy; the test is whether the ANSWER stays grounded and on-topic.

questions.question: List every cure or favor reported in 1933 and how each turned out.
questions.ground_truth: Notebook entries dated to 1933 (year from the page archival date) that record a reported outcome ('Reports ... recovered/cured/improved'). Each has an enrollment date and a later report date (bitemporal).
questions.notes: Aggregate + temporal + OUTCOME. The router should classify this 'complex' (markers: 'every', 'list'). Tests recall over a full year and the enrolled-vs-reported date pair.

questions.question: What does the archive record about Grace Panyard?
questions.ground_truth: Mentions of Grace Panyard across entries/letters. Requires resolving 'Grace.' (abbreviated) and OCR variants of 'Panyard' to one person.
questions.notes: Named-entity exact-match — a case where BM25 (lexical) should shine on the surname while entity resolution catches the abbreviated/variant given name (RESEARCH_PLAN A3).

questions.question: Find every mention of the O'Donnell family.
questions.ground_truth: All O'Donnell mentions, accounting for OCR variants (ODonnell, O Donnell, O'Donnel). A family cluster, not a single person.
questions.notes: Apostrophe + OCR-variant robustness. The tokenizer keeps apostrophes (O'Donnell) on purpose; this checks that variant spellings don't sink recall.

questions.question: Were there petitions on behalf of sick children?
questions.ground_truth: Entries where a parent/relative enrolls a child (son, daughter, baby) for an illness. Tests the RELATION (advocate -> beneficiary) plus a CONDITION.
questions.notes: Semantic, not lexical: 'sick children' rarely appears verbatim; the system must match 'her little boy', 'infant', 'my daughter's fever'. Good HyDE / dense-retrieval test.

questions.question: Did anyone ask Solanus for help with a drinking problem?
questions.ground_truth: Behavioral-condition petitions (alcohol / 'drink' / intemperance). A faithful answer cites the specific entries or abstains.
questions.notes: A behavioral CONDITION (not medical). Tests whether the system stays grounded on a sensitive topic and doesn't over-generalize from one entry.

questions.question: What conversions or returns to the faith were reported?
questions.ground_truth: Spiritual-favor entries: a lapsed person returning to the sacraments, a conversion, a reconciliation — distinct from medical cures.
questions.notes: FAVOR/OUTCOME of the *spiritual* kind. Precision test: must separate spiritual favors from the far more numerous medical ones.

questions.question: Which letters were addressed to Capuchin priests or the monastery?
questions.ground_truth: Letters whose recipient is a Capuchin friar / the monastery (ORG = Capuchin order, parishes). Recipient is a structured field on each letter.
questions.notes: ORG grounding using the structured 'recipient' field that already exists per letter (RESEARCH_PLAN B: structured fields are a free head-start).
